course_name: Fundamentals of Computer Systems and Networks

course_profile.one_sentence_summary: A foundational course on the architecture, protocols, and practical configuration of computer networks using Cisco Packet Tracer.
course_profile.short_summary: This course covers the theoretical principles and practical aspects of computer networking. Students learn about the OSI and TCP/IP models, network topologies, routing algorithms, and physical communication media. Extensive practical labs utilizing Cisco Packet Tracer and Cisco IOS focus on configuring switches, routers, DHCP/DNS services, dynamic routing (RIP, EIGRP, OSPF), ACLs, NAT, and wireless networks.

theoretical_understanding: Understand the principles of multi-layer network architectures, specifically the OSI and TCP/IP models.
Understand physical line characteristics, modulation, and data encoding methods in networks.
Comprehend the fundamental algorithms of network routing (distance vector and link-state) and switching.
practical_implementation: Configure network interfaces, IP addresses, and routing protocols (RIP, EIGRP, OSPF) using Cisco IOS Command Line Interface.
Implement network address translation (NAT) and dynamic host configuration protocols (DHCP).
Deploy basic network security using standard and extended Access Control Lists (ACL).
analysis_validation: Analyze network topologies and traffic flows in real-time simulation environments.
Diagnose and troubleshoot connectivity issues and network component misconfigurations.
architecture_design: Design and model local area networks (LANs) and wireless networks within simulation software.

implementation_tasks: Interconnecting network components (routers, switches, hubs, PCs) in a simulator.
Assigning IP spaces and subnet masks.
Executing Cisco IOS commands to configure protocols and services.
Validating network connectivity via simulation modes.

curricular_relations.reason: Knowledge of the Cisco IOS CLI is required to implement routing protocols on Cisco equipment.
Setting up DHCP scopes and DNS routing requires a firm grasp of IP address allocation and subnetting.
Graph theory forms the mathematical basis for shortest-path routing algorithms like OSPF.

what_student_can_understand: How data traverses local and global networks through different layers of the OSI model.
How IP addressing, subnetting, and routing algorithms function to direct traffic.
The differences between various network transmission technologies (Ethernet, Wi-Fi).
what_student_can_build: Simulated enterprise-like network infrastructures using Cisco Packet Tracer.
Configured network routers and switches providing dynamic routing, DHCP, and secure access.
what_student_can_apply: Cisco IOS CLI commands for device administration.
Diagnostic strategies to identify and fix network connection issues.
